passages.clozeText: A chord is formed when two or more different notes are played together.
Pitch moves upwards in an ascending melody.
A main voice supported by other instruments is accompanied.
Blues often uses a 12-bar chord pattern, while Jazz often features improvisation.
Opening and closing bellows produces the sound of an accordion.
A note that receives extra emphasis has an accent.
An acoustic guitar has six strings and a hollow body that helps amplify its sound.
When different notes sound together, they create harmony.
Music may have two, three or four beats in each bar.
Small groups and big bands can both perform Jazz.
Accelerando tells the performer to become gradually faster.
After a temporary change of speed, A tempo means return to the previous tempo.
The notes of a broken chord are played one after another rather than together.
Moving from one key to another is called a change of key.
In a canon, another part enters later with the same melody.
The lowest standard female voice is alto, below soprano.
A concerto may include a solo display section called a cadenza.
Backing vocals support the lead singer, often by adding harmony.
Harpsichord and basso continuo are common features of Baroque music.
Music from a range of African traditions is described as African music.
Arco tells string players to use the bow.
Voices singing without instrumental accompaniment perform a cappella.
An aria is a solo song in an opera or oratorio.
A Bothy ballad is a strophic folk song associated with farm workers in North-East Scotland.
Music with no established tonal centre is atonal.
Binary form has an A section followed by a contrasting B section.
An Alberti bass uses the broken-chord pattern lowest, highest, middle, highest.
Different rhythmic patterns sounding together can create cross rhythms.
In compound time, each dotted-crotchet beat divides into three quavers.
In a major key, chord I is the tonic and chord V is the dominant.
Chamber music includes string quartets and piano trios with independent instrumental parts.
Whole-tone scales and delicate orchestration can suggest an Impressionist style.
A short, crushed grace note before the main note is an acciaccatura.
An added sixth chord combines a triad with the note six scale steps above its root.
In 3 against 2, three equal notes occur in the same time as two equal notes.
Lengthening every note value of a theme in the same proportion is augmentation.
In basso continuo, a bass instrument plays the bass line and a chordal instrument supplies harmony.
A concerto grosso contrasts the concertino with the larger ripieno.
Rapid scales, leaps and vocal ornaments are features of coloratura.
Concerto grosso is a Baroque concerto featuring a small group of soloists.
An anthem is an English sacred choral work with a religious text.
A simple song or melody may be called an ayre or air.
An appoggiatura takes a significant part of the following main note’s value.
Raising the fifth of a major triad by a semitone creates an augmented triad.
In hemiola, two groups of three can be regrouped as three groups of two.
In a fugue, the next voice restates the subject as the answer.
Antiphonal music has separated groups that answer each other.
An ensemble of instruments, especially in Renaissance music, is a consort.
A high adult male voice using mainly falsetto is a countertenor.
